points.heading: What we learned
points.body:
Main idea: In this block, connect overview to a concrete example. A Spanish verb names an action. To conjugate means to change it for the person who acts. An infinitive is the dictionary form, such as cantar. The stem is what remains after -ar, and the ending is the part we add. Cantar belongs to the -ar family.

Explore: In cantar, cant- is the stem. Cant- plus -o makes yo canto; plus -as makes tú cantas; plus -a makes él canta. Hablar follows the same pattern: hablo, hablas, habla. Read the example again, then explain it in your own words before you begin the task.

Practice: First explain the idea in your own words. Then write two complete sentences that name the idea and give its example.

Common mistake: Do not repeat a label without explaining what it means.

points.heading: Let's practice point 1
points.body:
Main idea: In this block, connect point 1 to a concrete example. Comer is an infinitive in the Spanish -er family. Its stem is com-, and its present endings for yo, tú, and él are -o, -es, and -e.

Explore: Com- plus -o makes yo como; plus -es makes tú comes; plus -e makes él come. Beber works in the same way: bebo, bebes, bebe. Read the example again, then explain it in your own words before you begin the task.

Practice: First explain the idea in your own words. Then write two complete sentences that name the idea and give its example.

Common mistake: Do not repeat a label without explaining what it means.
